title: kbtools.py names the backlog.py subcommand that answers a which-tool question, such as the landing step durations
goal: kbtools.py 'which tool shows how long each landing step took' names backlog.py landings among its first three lines

run:
import subprocess as s,sys
p=s.run([sys.executable,"_tools/kbtools.py","which tool shows how long each landing step took"],capture_output=True,text=True)
top=p.stdout.splitlines()[:3];print(p.returncode,top)
sys.exit(0 if p.returncode==0 and any("backlog.py landings" in x for x in top) else 1)

clauses.clause: kbtools.py 'which tool shows how long each landing step took' names backlog.py landings among its first three lines

notes: From the 2026-10-24 telemetry and query-log analysis: the query log judged 'which tool shows how long each landing step took' missed this week (1 of 3 which-tool questions in 7 days; kbtools.py is called 140 times a week): kb_ask --route sends it to kind tools, but kbtools.py prints kb-lookup, kb_show and kb-sprint first and no line names backlog.py landings. backlog.py has 48 subcommands and one catalog line; in a probe that used each of 13 subcommands' own help text as the question, 11 (brief, dispatch, stage-back, procs, ops, landings, own, selfcheck, upstream-report, upstream-import, config) did not bring backlog.py into the top three lines (biased: some are answered by a skill or an MCP tool). Saves a few turns a week and a model lookup per miss. The subcommand-level gap of EP-5mp6pwnn (an agent finds the deterministic tool from one entry point); the ranking bugs BG-il5fgxps and BG-mqhzivkk are different. Also wanted: every subcommand named in a tool's usage block is findable by two of its own help words.
